front.title: Identity Streams: Per-Trait Source Attribution for Inferred and Stated Identity Claims

abstract.t: When one system tells another about a trait it has inferred about a person, the receiver today learns the trait and a confidence, and nothing about what the inference was drawn from. Because the receiver cannot tell a trait the person stated in answer to a question from one read off the person's activity on a linked platform, it cannot apply the lawful basis, consent and context limits that belong to each. This document defines a source tag carried with every inferred trait on the wire. The tag names, for each stream that contributed to the trait, a registered stream class, the provenance class of the observation, where the inference was computed, the lawful basis and purposes the stream was consented for, and the contexts the trait may be used in. It reuses the provenance- class vocabulary of the Morning Brief specification, establishes a registry of stream classes, and states the rules a receiver follows, including refusing a trait whose sources it cannot check. The same tag carries facts the person states about themselves, such as when they are available or the terms on which they offer something, and those facts keep the limits of the stream they were given on. It defines a wire field only. How traits are inferred, stored or scored is out of scope.
